topIssues.title: checkSpanBatch does not enforce activation-block user-tx rule that checkSingularBatch enforces
topIssues.author: trasnake87
topIssues.body:
`op-node/rollup/derive/batches.go` enforces the activation-block "no user transactions" rule (per spec [optimism/specs#791](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/791) and issue #17704) for singular batches but not for span batches. The same activation block, encoded as a span batch, is accepted.

### Where

`checkSingularBatch` (batches.go around L137) drops the batch:

```go
if (cfg.IsJovianActivationBlock(batch.Timestamp) ||
    cfg.IsKarstActivationBlock(batch.Timestamp) ||
    cfg.IsInteropActivationBlock(batch.Timestamp)) &&
    len(batch.Transactions) > 0 {
    log.Warn("dropping batch with user transactions in fork activation block")
    return BatchDrop
}
```

`checkSpanBatch` (batches.go L308–L445) validates timestamps, sequencer drift, deposit/SetCode tx exclusion per block, but never checks `IsJovianActivationBlock` / `IsKarstActivationBlock` / `IsInteropActivationBlock` against `batch.GetBlockTransactions(i)`.

History: PR #14797 added the rule for Isthmus (singular only, closed), PR #17984 added it for Jovian (singular only, merged), PR #19250 added Karst to the same condition (singular only, merged). PR #19150 separately added the SetCode check to span (`fix(op-node): add SetCodeTxType check to span batch validation`) — same kind of singular/span asymmetry, fixed in isolation. The activation-block rule appears to have been missed across all three iterations.

### Reproduction

A short unit test against `CheckBatch` builds the same activation-block user transaction twice — singular returns `BatchDrop`, span returns `BatchAccept`:

```go
package derive

import (
    "context"
    "math/big"
    "math/rand"
    "testing"

    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-core/forks"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-node/rollup"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/eth"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/testutils"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/common/hexutil"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/core/types"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/log"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestSpanBatchActivationBlockUserTx(t *testing.T) {
    rng := rand.New(rand.NewSource(0x51a75))
    chainID := big.NewInt(10)
    signer := types.NewLondonSigner(chainID)
    tx := testutils.RandomTx(rng, big.NewInt(1_000_000_000), signer)
    txData, err := tx.MarshalBinary()
    require.NoError(t, err)

    for _, fork := range []forks.Name{forks.Jovian, forks.Karst, forks.Interop} {
        t.Run(string(fork), func(t *testing.T) {
            l1A := eth.L1BlockRef{Hash: testutils.RandomHash(rng), Number: 100, Time: 1_000}
            l2Safe := eth.L2BlockRef{
                Hash: testutils.RandomHash(rng), Number: 200, Time: l1A.Time,
                L1Origin: l1A.ID(), ParentHash: testutils.RandomHash(rng),
            }
            cfg := &rollup.Config{
                Genesis:           rollup.Genesis{L2Time: l2Safe.Time},
                BlockTime:         2,
                SeqWindowSize:     4,
                MaxSequencerDrift: 30,
            }
            activationTime := l2Safe.Time + cfg.BlockTime
            cfg.ActivateAt(fork, activationTime)

            singular := &SingularBatch{
                ParentHash: l2Safe.Hash, EpochNum: rollup.Epoch(l1A.Number),
                EpochHash: l1A.Hash, Timestamp: activationTime,
                Transactions: []hexutil.Bytes{txData},
            }
            singularValidity := CheckBatch(context.Background(), cfg, log.New(),
                []eth.L1BlockRef{l1A}, l2Safe,
                &BatchWithL1InclusionBlock{L1InclusionBlock: l1A, Batch: singular}, nil)
            require.Equal(t, BatchValidity(BatchDrop), singularValidity)

            span := initializedSpanBatch([]*SingularBatch{{
                ParentHash: l2Safe.Hash, EpochNum: rollup.Epoch(l1A.Number),
                EpochHash: l1A.Hash, Timestamp: activationTime,
                Transactions: []hexutil.Bytes{txData},
            }}, cfg.Genesis.L2Time, chainID)

            spanValidity := CheckBatch(context.Background(), cfg, log.New(),
                []eth.L1BlockRef{l1A}, l2Safe,
                &BatchWithL1InclusionBlock{L1InclusionBlock: l1A, Batch: span}, nil)
            require.Equal(t, BatchValidity(BatchAccept), spanValidity,
                "span batches bypass activation-block user tx filtering")
        })
    }
}
```

`go test ./op-node/rollup/derive -run TestSpanBatchActivationBlockUserTx -v` passes for jovian, karst, and interop on `develop` (verified at `be742e31a`).

### Suggested fix

Apply the same condition inside `checkSpanBatch`'s per-block loop, before the per-tx validation:

```go
if (cfg.IsJovianActivationBlock(blockTimestamp) ||
    cfg.IsKarstActivationBlock(blockTimestamp) ||
    cfg.IsInteropActivationBlock(blockTimestamp)) &&
    len(batch.GetBlockTransactions(i)) > 0 {
    log.Warn("dropping span batch with user transactions in fork activation block")
    return BatchDrop
}
```

For symmetry with `checkSingularBatch` and consistency with the spec rule.

### Notes

The action test `TestActivationBlockTxOmission` added in #17984 uses `helpers.NewBatcherCfg()` which produces span batches by default (Delta+ fork, `ForceSubmitSingularBatch=false` → `useSpanChannelOut=true`). I have not run that test against current `develop`; if it currently passes, there is an additional path catching this that I have missed.

topIssues.title: op-node: do not retry publish failures that cannot succeed
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
Follow-up to #22585, which gave the async gossiper a bounded publish queue with retry-at-the-front.

## Problem

A block publish can fail **permanently**, and the gossiper currently cannot tell.

`Topic.Publish` runs op-node's own block validator **inline and synchronously on the publishing node** — `ValidateLocal` → `validate(..., local=true)`, and at `go-libp2p-pubsub@v0.17.0/validation.go:337`: `// run validation synchronously if it's a local publish`. So a publish can fail in ~1ms with no network I/O at all, and deterministically:

- bad block hash, oversized block, fork-shape mismatch, wrong `P2PSequencerAddress` (`op-node/p2p/gossip.go:292-449`)
- a block whose timestamp has aged past `--p2p.gossip.timestamp.threshold` (`gossip.go:356-360`)
- SSZ encode failure (`gossip.go:630`, `:634`)
- nil p2p signer (`op-node/node/node.go:767`), `signer is closed`, `pubsub.ErrTopicClosed`

Because #22585 retries at the front of the queue, such a block burns up to `maxPublishQueue` attempts and **head-of-line blocks every descendant for ~64s** (at a 2s block time) before queue pressure evicts it. Retrying is worse than futile for the staleness case in particular: a retry only ever makes a block *older*, so each attempt is strictly more hopeless than the last.

A second case falls out of the same trace: `RejectValidationIgnored` fires on any re-publish of a block that already passed local validation, and the gossiper's `isPending` dedup does not cover it (a block that published successfully and was then cleared can be re-queued). That is really "already out", but today it surfaces as an error, is counted as `publishing_errors`, and is retried.

## Proposal

Have the producer say whether a failure is permanent, and have the gossiper drop those immediately.

Follow the existing convention for classified errors in this repo — a wrapping sentinel matched with `errors.Is`, as `op-node/rollup/derive/error.go` does with `ErrTemporary` / `ErrReset` / `ErrCritical`. Declare `async.ErrPermanentPublish`, and wrap in `op-node/p2p/gossip.go` and `op-node/node/node.go`.

No import cycle stands in the way: `op-node/p2p` does **not** import `op-node/rollup/async` (`go list -deps`), and `async`'s whole dependency set is `op-service/bigs` + `op-service/eth`. The cycle its `Network`/`Metrics` comments guard against is `async ← rollup/driver`, a different edge — so no duck-typed interface is needed.

### The trap to avoid

Classification must be an **allowlist**, never a catch-all. `Topic.Publish` also returns `ctx.Err()` from its eval loop and from `sendMsgBlocking`, so the gossiper's own `publishTimeout` surfaces as `context.DeadlineExceeded` *through the same call*. A catch-all would mark a timed-out publish permanent and silently disable retry altogether. Worth a dedicated regression test.

### Known tradeoff

`pubsub.ValidationError.Reason` is `"validation failed"` for every reject, so the one self-healing check — `gossip.go:362-366`, timestamp more than 5s in the future — cannot be isolated from the error. Treating all rejects as permanent is proposed anyway, because a self-published block realistically cannot trip it: L2 timestamps are chain-derived (`nextL2Time := l2Parent.Time + BlockTime`, `op-node/rollup/derive/attributes.go:119`), sealing is scheduled `sealingDuration` (50ms) *before* `payloadTime`, the sequencer waits rather than sealing early when the head is ahead, and the validator runs in the same process off the same clock. Reaching it needs a backwards clock step or a `sealingDuration` above 5s.

## Notes

This does **not** remove the need for `retryInterval` or the attempt backstop added in #22585: a refused signer connection fails in microseconds and is legitimately transient, so the spin guard still earns its place, and stopped block production plus a refused signer is still 1 Hz forever without the backstop. This is a layer on top, not a simplification.

Discussion: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22585#discussion_r3937626460

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: enable ETHLockbox on every chain
topPRs.author: 0xOneTony
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Enables an `ETHLockbox` on every OP chain, regardless of whether interop or a custom gas token is enabled.
Today only interop chains use a lockbox. Making the lockbox universal is the prerequisite for #22093, which will make it the pause identifier for the shared contracts. This PR does not change how any contract resolves pause state or the guardian.

Changes

- OPCMv2 `upgrade()` and `deploy()` load or deploy, initialize, authorize, and enable an `ETHLockbox` for every chain. Existing chains without a lockbox pass the `ETHLockbox` permitted proxy deployment instruction.
- The portal's ETH is migrated into the lockbox when the feature is first enabled. Repeat upgrades do not migrate again, and chains in an interop set keep their shared lockbox.
- `OptimismPortal2.migrateLiquidity()` requires a configured lockbox instead of interop and reverts on custom gas token chains.
- `ETH_LOCKBOX` can no longer be disabled. Enabling it is blocked only while a pause is active on the `OptimismPortal` identifier.
- `StandardValidator` (`LOCKBOX-00`, `LOCKBOX-05`) and `ChainAssertions` (`CHECK-OP2-80`, `CHECK-OP2-85`) require the feature and a nonzero lockbox.
- Updates contract snapshots and tests.
Custom gas token chains get an enabled lockbox but keep gas-token custody in the portal. Their portal balances are not migrated.

Safety considerations

- Legacy ETH liquidity is migrated only on first activation; repeated upgrades do not migrate again.
- `upgrade()` never creates a second lockbox for a chain that already has one.
- `SystemConfig.paused()` already selects the lockbox identifier when the feature is on, so enabling the feature moves a chain's scoped pause key from its portal to its lockbox at upgrade time. Deputy pause configuration and monitoring keyed on the portal address need updating. An active portal-scoped pause blocks the upgrade; a global pause is unaffected.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22770

topPRs.title: op-reth: add chain head gas and base fee metrics
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## Description

op-geth exposes gas and fee attributes of the canonical head as `chain_head_basefee`, `chain_head_gas_used` and `chain_head_blob_gas_used` (plus `*_hist` histograms). op-reth had no equivalent, so operators migrating off op-geth lose that visibility — including the DA-footprint-per-block view those metrics were added for.

This adds them to op-reth.

### Prior art in op-geth

| what | op-geth PR | motivation |
|---|---|---|
| `chain/head/basefee` | [op-geth#658](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/658) | "Building block for calldata footprint limit" |
| `chain/head/gas_used`, `chain/head/blob_gas_used` + histograms | [op-geth#705](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/705) | "track the DA footprint per block", closes [optimism#17501](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17501) |

op-geth#705 encapsulated all of them into `core/blockchain_optimism.go`'s `updateOptimismBlockMetrics`, which is the surface this PR mirrors.

## Metric names

reth's Prometheus recorder applies a global `reth_` prefix ([`PrefixLayer::new("reth")`](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/main/crates/node/metrics/src/recorder.rs)), so exact name parity is not achievable. Using the `chain.head` scope gets as close as possible — the names differ from op-geth only by that prefix:

| op-geth | op-reth (this PR) |
|---|---|
| `chain_head_basefee` | `reth_chain_head_basefee` |
| `chain_head_gas_used` | `reth_chain_head_gas_used` |
| `chain_head_blob_gas_used` | `reth_chain_head_blob_gas_used` |
| `chain_head_gas_used_hist` | `reth_chain_head_gas_used_hist` |
| `chain_head_blob_gas_used_hist` | `reth_chain_head_blob_gas_used_hist` |

The block-height counterparts of op-geth's `chain/head/*` family already exist upstream and are unchanged here: `reth_blockchain_tree_canonical_chain_height`, `reth_blockchain_tree_safe_block_height`, `reth_blockchain_tree_finalized_block_height`.

## Implementation

`OpChainHeadMetrics` is driven from the canonical state notification stream, spawned once in `OpAddOns::launch_add_ons` so every op-reth node gets it. That placement deliberately avoids the launcher paths in `proof_history.rs`, which carry a "Keep in sync" warning about duplication with the sdm-fixture node.

Attributes a header does not carry are left unrecorded rather than reported as zero — matching op-geth's `TryUpdate`/`TryUpdateUint64` helpers. A pre-1559 chain does not publish a 0 base fee, and a pre-4844 chain does not skew the blob gas histogram with zeroes.

### Known gap

Canonical state notifications are not emitted on the backfill/pipeline-sync path, so these gauges do not advance during backfill. They begin tracking once the node follows the chain via the engine API. Head *gas* figures during backfill are of limited use anyway, but calling it out explicitly since op-geth updates its equivalents from `InsertHeaderChain` too.

## Tests

`cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --lib` — 31 passed, 0 failed.

The new unit test asserts both the recorded values and that a pre-Cancun header produces **no** blob gas observation. It was verified to fail against a deliberately broken implementation (`unwrap_or_default()` instead of the `Option` guard), which produces `Histogram([0.0])` instead of `Histogram([])`.

`cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-node --all-features --all-targets` and `cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check` are both clean.

## Follow-up

The op-reth Grafana dashboard in `grafana-dashboards` currently plots `chain_head_block` / `chain_head_header` / `chain_head_receipt` for op-geth; adding panels for these new series is a separate PR in that repo.

topPRs.author: pcw109550
topPRs.body: ## Description Mintlify's `` component is built for nested object fields in API reference pages and prepends "Show" / "Hide" to its title. The docs used it for FAQs, prerequisite blocks, flag references, and sample payloads, so on the live site toggles rendered as: ``` Show How often are subblocks produced? Show What is double-spending? Show --l1-eth-rpc ``` This PR switches every `` in `docs/public-docs` to ``, the component Mintlify recommends for general collapsible content and the one `governance/gov-faq.mdx` already uses. The header now shows the bare title with a chevron. The Subblocks FAQ additionally wraps each subsection in an `` so the questions stack in one panel. Content and links are unchanged. Every converted tag carried only a `title` attribute, and the diff is the tag rename plus indentation on the Subblocks page. ## Tests Verified against the live site: the deployed `op-stack/features/subblocks` page emits `Show ` for all seven FAQ entries, while the deployed `governance/gov-faq` page (Accordion) renders titles with no prefix. Grep confirms no `Expandable` remains under `docs/public-docs`. The Mintlify preview on this PR should show the new headers. ## Additional context Review agents: the diff touches only `.mdx` files, so none of the repo review agents (Go, Rust, CI config, deletion, StandardValidator, reth) match. No general code review was run; the change is a mechanical component swap with no prose edits. Prev(from https://docs.optimism.io/op-stack/features/subblocks): After:

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: verify StandardValidator sub-contract references in VerifyOPCM
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
`VerifyOPCM` marked two `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator` getters as `SKIP`:

```solidity
validatorGetterChecks["standardValidatorUtils"] = "SKIP";
validatorGetterChecks["migrationValidator"] = "SKIP";
```

Every other `SKIP` in that block is commented with `// Address verified via bytecode comparison` comment and is genuinely covered elsewhere, because `_getOpcmPropertyRefs` walks the `opcm`-prefixed getters on the OPCM itself and bytecode-compares each one. 

These addresses are stored in the `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator` rather than the OPCM, so that walk never reaches them. 

This adds a `BYTECODE:<ContractName>` check type that resolves the address from the getter  and uses `_verifyContractRef` to check it.
